messages:
incident-bot: SEV2 alert: multiple pods in namespace 'inference-prod' entering CrashLoopBackOff on nodes us-east-gpu-7/8/9. Root cause suspected: SIGSEGV in runtime_engine (runtime_engine.so). Paging oncall_sam and SRE.

pagerduty-bot: Pager duty: oncall_sam assigned (escalation: default rotation).

oncall_sam: Ack. Watching logs now. Which model/pools affected?

support_elaine: Noted customer reports: MuseChat (enterprise, dedicated-us-east) and internal staging saw elevated 500s starting ~08:00 UTC. Support opened tickets.

sre_mai: I'm seeing a pattern: OOMs on GPUs followed by driver resets, then segfaults in runtime_engine during graph execution. Crash signature points at fused_attention module in runtime. Collecting core dumps and journal logs.

eng_runtime_lee: I rolled a debug build to capture more info but agree initial evidence shows allocator path in fused kernel. We recently shipped a micro-optimization for temp buffer pooling. Could be unsafe when driver recovers mid-allocation.

eng_ml_nina: Also saw heavy KV-cache prefetch and large batch volume in metrics at 07:59. Prefetch + aggressive batching could oversubscribe vram. Maybe two-hit failure: memory pressure -> driver reset -> corrupted state -> segfault.

oncall_sam: Grabbed container log from a crash:

```
[2026-11-03T08:02:07Z] runtime-engine[2245]: model load starbridge-13b
[2026-11-03T08:02:09Z] runtime-engine[2245]: allocator: reserved 3.2G workspace
[2026-11-03T08:02:11Z] runtime-engine[2245]: CUDA: out of memory, driver reported reset
[2026-11-03T08:02:11Z] runtime-engine[2245]: segfault at 0x7f9b2f1c (runtime_engine.so+0x45b0)
```

infra_tom: Node dmesg shows GPU reset and nv-faults on gpu0. We should isolate node to prevent cascading restarts.

oncall_sam: Mitigation plan proposal
- Evacuate pods from nodes 7/8/9 and cordon them
- Temporarily disable KV prefetch and reduce max-batch-size for starbridge-13b
- Route dedicated-us-east traffic to fallback model starbridge-6b for affected orgs
- Roll runtime-engine to previous stable image v3.4.2 (revert pooled-buf change)
- Reboot nodes after pods drained if driver recoveries persist

sre_mai: +1. Also recommend setting per-pod GPU memory request limits (soft) to reduce oversubscribe while we triage.

eng_runtime_lee: I'll prepare the rollback image and push. Also enabling core collection for crashed pods to S3 for detailed analysis.

oncall_sam: Executing now:

```
kubectl cordon us-east-gpu-7
kubectl drain us-east-gpu-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
kubectl -n inference-prod set env deploy/starbridge-13b KV_PREFETCH=off
kubectl -n inference-prod set resources deploy/starbridge-13b --limits='nvidia.com/gpu=1'
kubectl -n inference-prod set image deploy/runtime-engine runtime-engine=registry.redwood/runtime-engine:v3.4.2
kubectl -n inference-prod rollout status deploy/runtime-engine
```

oncall_sam: Drained two nodes, third node 9 has a stuck pod on volume detach. infra_tom taking a look.

infra_tom: Forced detach and restarted kubelet on node 9. Node drained.

oncall_sam: Rollout complete — most runtime-engine pods are OK. CrashLoop count reduced from 14 -> 3. Those 3 are on the previously reset node and show repeated driver recovery in dmesg.

support_elaine: Customer update: MuseChat reports errors dropped significantly after 12 minutes, still seeing occasional timeouts. CS requested ETA on full recovery.

perf_ash: Flag: revert will slightly increase median latency for some routes (v3.4.2 doesn't have pooled buffer optimization). Need to quantify impact.

eng_runtime_lee: Pulled cores and ran gdb on one coredump. Backtrace points to fused_attention::forward -> cuda_malloc -> driver_reset_handler -> segfault on nullptr deref. Suspect allocator didn't clear state after driver reset.

```
#0  0x00007faeab12b45c in fused_attention::forward() at fused_attention.cu:502
#1  0x00007faeab0f3f10 in graph_executor::run() at executor.cpp:810
#2  0x00007faeab0e9a01 in worker_thread::main() at worker.cpp:189
```

sre_mai: We've applied the routing fallback for orgs on Dedicated-us-east to starbridge-6b. Traffic shift ~40%. Error-rate for MuseChat now within SLA thresholds.

oncall_sam: Node 9 rebooted as a precaution. After reboot, GPU driver appears stable and remaining runtime-engine pods recovered. Monitoring for 30m.

eng_ml_nina: I'll add a temporary throttle in the autoscaler to prevent rapid scaling of heavy-model replicas while we patch.

eng_runtime_lee: Action items I'm opening now:
- emergency PR to add safe-driver-reset handling in allocator + unit tests (lee)
- add feature-flag gating for pooled-buf optimization (lee)
- postmortem + customer timeline (elaine + sam)
- telemetry: correlate nv-faults + coredumps + model routing (mai)

support_elaine: I'll draft customer brief and include windows, mitigations, and planned timeline for re-enabling optimization.

perf_ash: Scheduling perf run comparing v3.4.2 vs v3.4.3 (with pooled-buf behind feature flag) in staging before next rollout.

sre_mai: Containment checklist:
- [x] Affected nodes cordoned/drained
- [x] Rollback runtime-engine to v3.4.2
- [x] KV prefetch disabled for starbridge-13b
- [x] Routing overrides applied
- [x] Node reboots completed and driver stable

incident-bot: Incident contained at 1801244890. Severity downgraded to SEV3 pending postmortem.

oncall_sam: Thanks all. I'll hand off to daytime team with notes and will be oncall backup until 10:00 UTC.

---
Note: thread contains logs, commands, and backtraces. Postmortem doc will be linked here when ready.
